desc: The lesser black-backed gull is a large gull that breeds on the Atlantic and Arctic coasts of Europe. It is migratory, wintering from the British Isles south to West Africa. However, it has increased dramatically in North America, especially along the east coast. Formerly just a winter visitor to North America, it now occurs in large numbers some winters and birds are recorded year-round. However, there is serious concern about decline in many parts of its range. The species is on the UK Amber List because the UK is home to 40 per cent of the European population and more than half of these are found at fewer than ten breeding sites.

La gaviota sombría es una especie de ave Charadriiforme de la familia Laridae. Es una de las gaviotas más comunes y más cosmopolitas del mundo. Ave migradora, se encuentra desde Groenlandia y Escandinavia hasta el Norte de África, donde hiberna. También se pueden ver hibernando en las costas norteamericanas a ejemplares procedentes de Islandia.

The white-bellied warbler was formerly treated as a separate species but is now considered to be conspecific with the golden-crowned warbler.

En México se le ha observado principalmente en la planicie costera del Golfo, en la vertiente del Pacífico y en la península de Yucatán. Studies in 1993, however, have indicated that bigfin reef squids may comprise several cryptic species, that are very similar and closely related.
